feeds.notes: Run 1 achieved a 5.12s interval against a 16s cadence, comfortably above Nyquist, so this is the one feed whose cadence is already a measured property rather than a sampling artefact. Degraded since 2026-06-04: its 64% 304 rate is inflated by a frozen upstream and is not a clean bytes-saved figure.

60s answers the open question about this feed -- whether validators are honoured -- because a GET with validators is what detects a false-200, and run 1 saw 0% 304 with one false-200 across only 16 requests. 60 samples settles it. ACCEPTED TRADE: at 60s the cadence stays below Nyquist and will again be flagged unresolved. Resolving it would need either far more GETs from a volunteer service, or HEAD sampling that cannot detect a false-200. Gate 0 does not depend on it.

Documented 15s cadence, 1.27 MB. 5s sampling puts Nyquist at 10s, below the documented cadence, so unlike gtfs.de this feed's cadence should resolve. Worst case if validators are ignored is ~914 MB/hour; ETag, Last-Modified and Cache-Control max-age=5 are all present, so most responses should be 304 and the real figure far lower.

The high-frequency shape. Documented 1s cadence at 122 KB, a workload unlike anything characterised so far (vbb 16s, ovapi <=60s, gtfs.de 30s), and the only candidate that will actually exercise a bounded queue before Gate 5 designs its backpressure. KNOWN LIMIT, recorded up front: 2s sampling puts Nyquist at 4s, so a genuine 1s cadence CANNOT be resolved and the analyser will correctly flag it. Resolving 1s would need sustained 2+ requests/second for an hour, which is not a reasonable ask of a public API. The measurable claim is "updates at least every 2s", read off the 200-vs-304 pattern, and that is sufficient to size a queue. Worst case ~220 MB/hour.
